key_insight: eMOOD replaces the usual troubled-cell test in MOOD with an entropy-production indicator, giving more targeted shock detection with fewer flagged cells.
engineering_relevance: This improves the efficiency and scalability of high-order finite-volume shock-capturing on unstructured meshes while preserving accuracy for challenging compressible-flow problems.
method: Use numerical entropy generation as a compact troubled-cell indicator instead of a relaxed discrete maximum principle.
Deploy the detector inside both a standard MOOD cascade and a MOOD-CWENO hybrid reconstruction strategy.
Implement and test the approach in the parallel UCNS3D solver for multiphase and shock-dominated flows.
evidence_signal: Across Shu-Osher, double Mach reflection, forward-facing step, shock-helium-bubble, and triple material point cases, the method reportedly flags up to 75% fewer cells and delivers up to 20% speed-up without loss of solution quality.
watch_item: Entropy-based detection is physically motivated, but its effectiveness may depend on robust entropy evaluation and careful tuning for different meshes and flow regimes.
paper_title: eMOOD: Entropy-Based Multidimensional Optimal Order Detection for High-Order Shock-Capturing Finite-Volume Schemes
